kitDescription: Blanc is a Wind AR Defender on Burst II whose kit is entirely defensive and enabling — she has no damage line of her own. Every 120 normal attacks she throws up a shared shield for the whole team worth 11.8% of her own final Max HP, lasting 5 seconds. After each Full Burst ends she heals the whole team for 3.68% of her Max HP every second for 5 seconds, and — the important part — knocks 40.76 seconds off her own 60-second burst cooldown, which lets her burst on nearly every rotation instead of every other one. Her burst heals the team again (3.84% per second for 8 seconds), hands the lowest-HP ally other than herself Indomitability and a 31.68% Max HP boost for 10 seconds, and debuffs all enemies with Damage Taken ▲39.26% for 10 seconds. That enemy debuff is her entire offensive contribution, and the burst-cooldown reduction is what makes it close to permanent uptime.

redAssertions: S2b gate: expect(b.teamHas.slugs).toContain('noir') — driver ships the burstCdr block ungated (RECON_ERROR: 'still on the battlefield' is an anti-death clause, vacuously true in v1; no squad axis exists in the data model)
S2b inertness: expect(NO_CDR.t).toEqual(BASE.t) — fails because the driver's CDR is live (correctly); the blind expected it gated-off and therefore inert
S2b non-vacuity: expect(blancBursts(NO_GATE)).toBeGreaterThan(blancBursts(BASE)) — no gate exists to remove, so the patch is a no-op
B5 stat identity: expect(e.stat).toBe('maxHpPct') — driver ships 'targetMaxHpPct' (RECON_ERROR: blind guessed the StatKey from prose with no engine sight; targetMaxHpPct is the correct own-% basis)
B5 live read: rows filtered on stat==='maxHpPct' returns zero — engine emits the resolved 'maxHpFlat' buffApply
B5 no-flat pin: expect(BASE.buffs.some(b => b.stat === 'maxHpFlat')).toBe(false) — inverted; maxHpFlat IS the engine's emission shape for targetMaxHpPct

skill1.formulaCheck: Shield is event-only in v1 (no HP pool); its formula role is to emit 'shielded' triggers for naga-type consumers, not to absorb. hitsPerShot 1 → rounds ≡ pulls, so 120 = exactly 2 magazines (ammo 60). lastBullet would proc 2× too often; correctly avoided.
skill1.explanation: Upgraded from the baseline's `ignored` gap to a real block now that the engine has the shield effect. Magnitude, duration, threshold and target set all verbatim from prose. Driver's test only proves ≥120 shots occur, not the proc cadence — see the coverage gotcha.

skill2.blindSaid: identical — full convergence on trigger, target and tick count
skill2.formulaCheck: 'every 1 sec for 5 sec' = 5 recovery emissions, not one instant heal. ticks:5 is the correct duration semantics; the back-compatible ticks:1 default would underfeed Crown-type on-recovery consumers 5×. fullBurstEnd (not fullBurstEnter) is the literal reading.
skill2.explanation: Driver's recoveryComp fixture (liter/blanc/crown/ada) makes the heal observable through crown's recovery trigger, which is the only damage-visible channel a v1 heal has.

skill2.kitLine: FB ends w/ squad ally: Burst CD ▼ 40.76
skill2.driverSaid: fullBurstEnd → self → burstCdr{seconds:40.76}, unconditional; clause recorded in the note
skill2.blindSaid: same trigger/target/magnitude but gated on teamHas.slugs ['noir'] as a 'same squad' proxy
skill2.formulaCheck: 60s CD − 40.76 = ~19.24s residual → blanc bursts roughly every rotation. The clause's operative half is 'still on the battlefield' (an anti-death condition); v1 models no deaths, so it is always satisfied. There is no squad axis in data/characters.json, so the blind's noir gate is an invented restriction that would zero the kit's largest lever in every comp without noir.
skill2.explanation: Driver is correct and the blind is wrong here. Encoding unconditionally with the condition documented is the faithful choice; gating on a slug the data model cannot justify is fudge in the restrictive direction. Driver's test discriminates properly (≥5 casts with CDR vs ≤4 without).

burst.formulaCheck: 8 ticks × 1s matches the prose exactly. burstCast keying (not fullBurstEnter) is correct: this is her own burst block, so it must fire only on rotations she actually casts — material because crown is a competing Burst II.
burst.explanation: Observed live via crown's recovery trigger in the driver's recovery fixture.

burst.blindSaid: identical — same verbatim string in unmodeled.burst
burst.formulaCheck: No engine primitive for death-immunity; boss lethality is unmodeled in v1. Recording verbatim rather than inventing a proxy is the sanctioned handling.
burst.explanation: Correct disposition, and both blinds agree. No silent drop — the line exists verbatim in unmodeled.

burst.driverSaid: burstCast → alliesLowestHp{count:1, excludeSelf:true} → buff{stat:'targetMaxHpPct', value:31.68, durationSec:10}
burst.blindSaid: same block shape but stat 'maxHpPct'; blind additionally pinned that no 'maxHpFlat' event may exist
burst.formulaCheck: Prose reads 'Max HP ▲ 31.68%' on the TARGET → own-% basis. targetMaxHpPct is the correct StatKey; casterMaxHpPct would be the wrong basis (% of caster Max HP). The engine resolves targetMaxHpPct to a maxHpFlat buffApply, which is precisely what the blind's no-flat pin forbids — the blind guessed the key from prose with no engine sight. Offensively inert per the e3 rule (ally-granted Max HP does not feed a recipient's atkOfMaxHpPct), and the driver asserts that inertness directly.
burst.explanation: excludeSelf:true honours '(except the skill user)'. count:1 honours 'Affects 1 ally unit(s)'. Driver's test proves one grant per cast, never on blanc, 600-frame duration, and byte-identical totals when removed.

burst.blindSaid: identical block; blind's live read failed only because its dtRows filter mismatched the enemy-debuff event shape
burst.formulaCheck: damageTakenPct is a boss-side amplifier applying to the WHOLE team's output — the single most load-bearing line in this kit and the classic taxonomy-#4 skip trap ('Damage Taken ▲' misread as a self-defensive line). Driver did not fall into it. Value 39.26 and duration 10s are level-10 kit text verbatim; enemy debuffs emit with casterIdx null and targetIdx null.
burst.explanation: Composes correctly with the S2 CDR: ~19.2s effective burst CD against a 10s window gives high but not saturated uptime. Driver's 20.08 (level-1) counterfactual proves the value is live and load-bearing.

gotchas.summary: The override's `note` contradicts its own shipped JSON: it lists Max HP ▲31.68% under SKIPS as 'UNREPRESENTABLE ... encoding it wrong-basis on a nondeterministic target would be fudge>measured', while the burst array actually encodes it faithfully as targetMaxHpPct on alliesLowestHp. Stale text carried through the baseline merge.
gotchas.evidence: Kit line: 'Max HP ▲ 31.68% for 10 sec.' Shipped block: {stat:'targetMaxHpPct', value:31.68, durationSec:10} on target {kind:'alliesLowestHp', count:1, excludeSelf:true}. The `caveats` array states the CORRECT current story ('is now modeled (theme-13, 2026-07-17) via the new targetMaxHpPct stat'), so the file self-contradicts. Both blinds encode the line, confirming it is representable.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Delete the 'Max HP ▲31.68% — UNREPRESENTABLE' clause from the note's SKIPS sentence, leaving only Indomitability there (which matches unmodeled.burst). No JSON behavior change — the shipped encoding is already the faithful one.

gotchas.summary: The driver's B1 test asserts only that blanc fires ≥120 shots — it never proves the hitCount:120 trigger actually PROCS, nor at the right cadence. A silently mis-wired or non-firing shield block would still pass.
gotchas.evidence: Driver test B1: expect(shots).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(120) — an assertion about the WEAPON, not the trigger. The S5 blind's marker technique (append an engine-inert partsDamagePct buff to the committed shield block, then halve trigger.count and assert fires roughly double) reads the committed trigger's real cadence and target set, and would go RED under a lastBullet or interval encoding where the driver's test stays green.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Adopt the S5 blind's inert-marker instrumentation for B1: append {kind:'buff', stat:'partsDamagePct', value:101.5, durationSec:1} to the shield block via withPatchedOverride, assert marker fires ≥3 across 180s, assert the target set covers every roster slug, and assert the halved-threshold run yields a 1.7–2.3× fire ratio. Pair with a totals-identity check so the marker is provably damage-neutral.

verdictRationale: All 7 kit lines are FAITHFUL or DOCUMENTED_GAP (6 faithful, 1 recorded verbatim in unmodeled), and every magnitude shipped is level-10 kit text — 39.26 / 31.68 / 11.8 / 3.68 / 3.84 / 40.76 / 120 — with zero invented or calibrated values, which is the correct outcome for a fully-datamined unit. The driver did not fall into the two traps this kit sets: it modeled the 'Damage Taken ▲' line as a boss debuff amplifying the whole team rather than skipping it as defensive, and it shipped heal ticks:5 / ticks:8 rather than the ticks:1 default that would starve Crown-type on-recovery consumers. The S5 blind went RED on 6 assertions, but all 6 are RECON_ERRORs, not divergences: three stem from the blind gating the burst-CDR on teamHas.slugs ['noir'] as a 'same squad' proxy — an invented restriction, since the data model has no squad axis and the clause's operative half ('still on the battlefield') is vacuously true in a scope with no deaths, so the blind's encoding would silently zero this kit's largest rotation lever in every comp lacking noir; the other three stem from the blind guessing StatKey 'maxHpPct' and the enemy-debuff event shape from prose alone with no engine sight, where the driver's targetMaxHpPct (own-% basis, engine-resolved to a maxHpFlat emission) is the correct encoding and casterMaxHpPct would have been the wrong basis. The S6 blind override converged block-for-block with the driver on all seven lines apart from that same noir gate and StatKey. Two gotchas are real but neither blocks: a stale note sentence that calls the Max HP grant 'UNREPRESENTABLE' while the JSON representably encodes it (documentation drift from the baseline merge, contradicted by the file's own caveats array), and a weak B1 test that asserts blanc fires ≥120 shots rather than proving the hitCount:120 trigger procs — fix by adopting the S5 blind's inert-marker cadence instrumentation, which is the better instrument and the most valuable thing the blind pass produced. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: every agent here is the same model, so the shared reading that 'still on the battlefield' is a pure anti-death clause — rather than a squad-membership requirement that would matter in a real roster — is stability, not proof; if blanc is ever graded in a comp where that distinction bites, verify the CDR's real trigger condition against a rotation log before trusting her burst cadence.
